title: The MESAS Project: Long-wavelength Follow-up Observations of Sirius A
question: What is the long-wavelength (1.4-9 mm) emission of Sirius A, and is it consistent with PHOENIX stellar atmosphere models and stable over time?

what.value: Previous JCMT, SMA, VLA long-wavelength data and PHOENIX LTE model of Sirius A

evidence.quote: Previous long wavelength observations of Sirius A are summarized in (cite: white18) and are shown in Fig. [1](#tb_plot) (black circles).

what.value: Sirius B Teff 25369 K and radius 0.008098 Rsun

evidence.quote: effective temperature of T$_{eff}=25369~\rm K$ and radius of $\rm 0.008098~R_{\odot}$ (cite: bond17)

what.value: Fomalhaut ALMA fluxes 1.79 mJy (0.87 mm) and 0.88 mJy (1.3 mm)

evidence.quote: observed a flux of 1.79 mJy and 0.88 mJy, respectively (cite: su16; white_fom)

recipe.goal: Fit point-source fluxes to ALMA and VLA visibilities
recipe.method: Point-source fit to visibilities per SPW with minimum chi-squared iteration
assumptions: Sirius A is a point source (0.00602")

recipe.method: Map of all GBT data, Gaussian fit at Sirius A position
Non-linear least squares fit of T_obs = C0 T_phot (lambda/0.45mm)^alpha over 0.45-9.0 mm
assumptions: Rayleigh-Jeans limit, T_obs substituted for T_B

evidence.quote: This yields a total flux of $0.90\pm0.11$ mJy.

answer_key.quantity: Predicted Fomalhaut flux at 0.87 and 1.3 mm

evidence.quote: yields a predicted flux of 1.88 mJy and 0.84 mJy for the 2 ALMA wavelengths, respectively.

not_stated_but_needed: uvmodelfit starting parameters and fit options
Which ALMA channels/SPWs were averaged and any flagging
ALMA imaging details (weighting, cell size, deconvolver, masks)
Data points and weights used in the power-law fit
Fitting range handling for Sirius B
missing_for_reproduction: Model spectrum values from White et al. 2018
score_reason: Simple point-source fits with public ALMA pipeline data, but several settings are unstated.
rediscovery_reason: Data are likely public, recipe is simple, and results are numeric fluxes.
